teacher_info.teaching_style:
My teaching style varies based on how the student learns best. Visual learners are individuals who prefer to take in their information visually—be that with maps, graphs, diagrams, charts, and others.
Auditory learners are individuals who learn better when they take in information in auditory form when it is heard or spoken. Kinesthetic learners are individuals who prefer to learn by doing. Reading/writing learners consume information best when it’s in words, whether that’s by writing it down or reading it. My goals are to make sure the students feel comfortable, valued, & inspired. I want them to feel excited to come to class, learn something new, and speak English with confidence and ease.

Finally, I spend most of my time abroad and am therefore familiar with the difficulties of communicating in a foreign language when you have not developed the necessary skills to communicate clearly and effectively. pro_course_detail.description:
“English for Daily Life” is about the vocabulary necessary in order to live in a foreign country, so the class is perfect for people who live in a foreign country or who are planning to move. I have lived in three different countries, so I know you will definitely need to be familiar with these topics.

We learn things like:
* Going to the doctor
* Calling the police
* Calling an ambulance
* Going to the dentist
* Going to the post office
* Going to the vet
* Buying something at the grocery store
* Calling the government
* Calling the immigration department
* Filling out forms and paperwork
* Insurance vocabulary
* Rental contracts
* Sending a letter
* Introducing yourself to your neighbors
* Many more!

Before class I will send you a list of topics and you can choose the ones you want to learn. I will send topic-related vocabulary and we will practice the vocabulary and dialogues during class together.  

If you want a class similar to those you took in school (with a focus on vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, and other skills) please schedule GENERAL ENGLISH. In General English classes, we learn topics like describing food, talking about hobbies, going on vacation, etc. "English for Daily Life" is about living and communicating when you live abroad.

2. Do activities to practice what we've learned. (Fill in the blank, complete the sentence, match the dialogue with a response, put vocabulary in a category, etc.)
3. Do a role play or have a conversation to use what we learned earlier and speak naturally.

Lessons teach all aspects of language, including grammar, pronunciation, vocabulary, conversational English, reading, and writing skills.

2009年，我住在台灣台北，在那裡學習了一個學期。
I began teaching in Taiwan in 2009, doing conversation groups at Shih Hsin University. This challenged me immediately, and I still look back on it as a period of growth. A few years later I had the honor and privilege to teach a semester in Korea at a kindergarten, dancing and singing the days away with some fun little ones!

Increase your fluency. 
Improve your pronunciation. 
Overcome your fear of speaking. 
Develop your listening comprehension.

Expand your vocabulary. 
Enjoy a relaxed and engaging conversation. 

Do you understand English better than you speak it? If so, you're not alone. One of the most common frustrations of even the most advanced English students is that they understand what they read and hear, but struggle to express themselves in spoken exchanges. Why? The answer is simple: language learners have more opportunities to read and listen to the language they’re learning than to speak or write it. However, the only way to improve your speaking skills is through practice, ideally with a native speaker. This is especially true of English, because fluency in English depends to a great degree on its peculiar patterns of stress and intonation.

In these lessons, you will get the practice you need to increase your fluency and reach your other English-related goals. We will get to know one another in a relaxed conversation about ourselves and about topics that interest you. I will provide prompts to help you if you’re not sure what you feel like talking about during the lesson. I will also provide constructive feedback and guidance, based on areas in which you have the most room for improvement. At the end of the lesson, you will have access to a feedback document that contains my notes on any errors you made and ways you can improve. This document can serve as a guide for the practice and study you do on your own, outside of lessons.
